recognize_zh: 箭頭指的漿細胞在細胞核位置上有兩個淡藍色、邊界清楚的圓形包涵體，看起來像疊在核上（核內假包涵體），即 Dutcher body；其他漿細胞也有細胞質內小空泡。
features: Plasma cell (arrow) with eccentric nucleus and basophilic cytoplasm containing two small, round, pale, sharply demarcated inclusions superimposed on the nucleus (Dutcher bodies)
Additional plasma cells with round clear cytoplasmic globules (Russell body-like) and a nuclear pale inclusion in a cell on the right
Mixed background of maturing granulocytes (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, band and segmented neutrophils), an eosinophil and erythroid precursors
Scattered small lymphocytes; aspirate is cellular
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular specimen with maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements and scattered plasma cells. The indicated plasma cell contains two small, round, pale-staining inclusions overlying the nucleus, representing Dutcher bodies (intranuclear cytoplasmic invaginations of immunoglobulin). Other plasma cells show clear round cytoplasmic globules. Dutcher bodies indicate immunoglobulin accumulation and are more often associated with a clonal plasma cell or lymphoplasmacytic neoplasm; correlation with plasma cell quantitation, light-chain restriction and serum protein studies is recommended.

ddx.vs: Russell bodies lie within the cytoplasm away from the nucleus, whereas Dutcher bodies project over the nucleus as apparent intranuclear inclusions.
Nucleoli are purple-blue and integral to chromatin, while Dutcher bodies are pale, glassy and sharply outlined.
Vacuoles overlying cytoplasm are clear and do not indent the nuclear outline, unlike the nuclear-superimposed Dutcher body.
